title: Warranty Information & Engineering Certifications
subtitle: Comprehensive 50-Year Structural Steel & 10-Year Weatherproofing Guarantee
content:
50-Year Structural Warranty

Every ModularHome structure is built with precision cold-formed galvanized steel trusses and framing members engineered to withstand hurricane winds (up to 150 MPH) and extreme snow loads (up to 50 PSF). Our structural frames are guaranteed against rust-through, rot, warping, and seismic failure for 50 full years.

What Is Covered

  • Structural Steel Frame: 50-year non-prorated structural integrity warranty.
  • Roofing & Thermal Envelope: 25-year manufacturer standing seam roof & weather barrier warranty.
  • Plumbing & Electrical: 10-year comprehensive factory-installed systems warranty.
  • Interior Fixtures & Appliances: Full manufacturer warranties passed directly to the homeowner.
  • Cosmetic Workmanship: 1-year comprehensive factory finish and fitment guarantee.

IBC & State Modular Certifications

All modular plans and finished modules carry stamped state engineering approvals and comply with all applicable International Building Codes (IBC) and International Residential Codes (IRC). Each home receives factory quality control stamps and state modular insignia before shipment.

title: Privacy Policy
subtitle: How ModularHome.com collects, uses, and protects your personal information
content:
Your Privacy Matters

At ModularHome.com, we respect your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data. This privacy policy describes how we collect, store, and process information when you browse our catalog, use our quotation tools, submit floor plans, or contact our customer team.

Information We Collect

  • Contact Information: Your name, email address, phone number, and delivery location/ZIP code.
  • Project Details: Preferred home styles, bedrooms, square footage requirements, budget range, and custom blueprint uploads.

title: Refund & Cancellation Policy
subtitle: Clear policies on digital floor plan licensing, design deposits, and factory order cancellations
content:
Refund & Cancellation Policy

At ModularHome.com, we strive for total transparency in all customer transactions. Please review our policies for digital products, custom architectural services, and factory build orders below.

1. Digital Floor Plans & CAD Blueprints

Due to the instant delivery nature of digital goods, floor plan PDF downloads and CAD file packages are non-refundable once downloaded. If you encounter any technical difficulty accessing your files, our support team will provide replacement downloads immediately.

2. Custom Architectural & Engineering Retainers

Initial design drafting retainers are 100% refundable within 48 hours of initial payment if drafting work has not yet commenced. Once structural engineering reviews or stamped blueprint drafting has begun, retainers are non-refundable but applicable as a credit toward your home order.

3. Factory Module Manufacturing Orders

  • Prior to Steel Framing Fabrication: Cancellation is subject to a 10% administrative and engineering fee, with the balance of your factory deposit refunded in full.
  • After Factory Fabrication Commences: Because modular homes are built to custom state and client specifications, in-progress factory orders cannot be refunded.

How to Request a Cancellation

Please submit written cancellation requests to support@modularhome.com with your order reference number and project address.

title: Shipping & Delivery Policy
subtitle: Nationwide freight logistics, oversized transport permits, and crane set coordination
content:
Shipping & Delivery Policy

ModularHome.com coordinates turnkey freight logistics for modular sections, steel barndominium kits, and prefab cabins across all 48 contiguous United States and Alaska.

1. Logistics & Oversized Transport

Modular units are transported via specialized heavy-duty lowboy trailers and escort vehicles. All oversized state department of transportation (DOT) permits, route surveys, and bridge clearances are managed by our logistics dispatch team.

2. Site Readiness & Delivery Requirements

  • Road Accessibility: Delivery access roads must accommodate 53-foot tractor-trailers with a minimum 14-foot overhead clearance (free of low tree branches and power lines).
  • Foundation Readiness: Permanent concrete foundation (crawlspace, basement, or engineered slab) must be fully cured and certified before delivery day.
  • Crane Set Zone: An unobstructed level zone of at least 30x40 feet is required for mobile crane placement and module offloading.

3. Delivery Inspection & Sign-off

A certified project manager or homeowner must be present during delivery and crane setting to perform the initial arrival walkthrough and sign the delivery verification bill of lading.
metaDescription: Read the ModularHome.com shipping and delivery guidelines for nationwide modular home freight and crane installation.

title: Accessibility Statement
subtitle: Our commitment to digital accessibility for all home buyers and visitors
content:
Accessibility Statement

ModularHome.com is dedicated to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continuously enhance the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards to our website and web applications.

Conformance Status

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) defines requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. ModularHome.com strives to conform with WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards.

Key Accessibility Features

  • High Color Contrast: Designed with clean typography and high contrast ratios for readability.
  • Keyboard Navigation: Full keyboard navigability across search filters, mega menus, and checkout wizards.
  • Alt Text & ARIA Labels: Meaningful alternative text on architectural imagery and descriptive ARIA attributes for screen readers.
  • Responsive Scalability: Seamless zoom and font enlargement without losing page layout or content clarity.

Feedback & Assistance

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of ModularHome.com. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please contact our support team at accessibility@modularhome.com or call +1 (812) 595-4033. We will work with you to provide the information or service you require through an accessible communication method.
metaDescription: ModularHome.com is committed to WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility. Learn about our accessibility standards and support.

title: Pricing & Packages

content:
Transparent Modular Home Pricing

At ModularHome.com, we believe you deserve straightforward pricing without hidden contractor markups. Because modular homes are built in climate-controlled factories with zero material waste, you save an average of 15% to 25% compared to traditional stick-built construction.

Package Comparison

Package Level Est. Price / Sq. Ft. What's Included
Structural Shell Kit $65 – $95 / sq.ft Engineered steel frame, exterior sheathing, roof trusses, standing seam metal roof, and stamped plans.
Dry-In Lockup Package $110 – $155 / sq.ft Shell kit + Low-E windows, exterior doors, weather barrier wrap, and rough-in plumbing & electrical chases.
Turnkey Move-In Ready $165 – $260 / sq.ft Fully finished interior, custom cabinetry, quartz countertops, luxury vinyl plank, appliances, HVAC, and crane installation.

What Influences Total Project Cost?

  • Site Preparation: Grading, tree clearing, driveway access, and soil engineering.
  • Foundation Type: Concrete slab, stem wall crawlspace, or full conditioned basement.
  • Utility Connections: Well & septic installation or municipal water, power, and sewer tie-ins.
  • Interior Finishes: Standard vs premium architectural upgrades, appliances, and fixtures.

title: Modular Home Financing Guide
subtitle: Construction-to-permanent loans, preferred modular lenders, and low-down-payment options
content:
How Modular Home Financing Works

Financing a factory-built modular home is virtually identical to financing a traditional custom site-built home. Because modular homes are built to local IBC building codes and permanently attached to real estate foundations, they qualify for standard residential mortgages and appraisal values.

Popular Financing Programs

  • Construction-to-Permanent Loans (One-Time Close): The most popular modular loan option. Combines land purchase, factory manufacturing draws, and site work into a single loan with only one set of closing costs. Automatically converts into a permanent 15- or 30-year fixed mortgage upon move-in.
  • FHA Construction Loans: Low down payment options (as low as 3.5%) for eligible borrowers building their primary modular residence.
  • VA Construction Loans: 0% down payment financing for eligible military veterans and active-duty service members.
  • USDA Rural Development Loans: 100% financing for modular home construction in designated rural and suburban areas.
  • Land Equity Rollover: If you already own your build site free and clear, your land value can count directly toward your construction loan down payment.

Step-by-Step Financing Process

  1. Pre-Qualification: Review your credit score and determine your total purchasing power.
  2. Model & Plan Selection: Choose your floor plan and receive an itemized manufacturing quote from ModularHome.com.
  3. Lender Underwriting & Appraisal: Your lender orders an appraisal based on your blueprints and comparable modular homes in your county.
  4. Construction Draws: The lender releases milestone disbursements as the factory completes framing, roofing, and delivery.
  5. Permanent Conversion: Final walkthrough is completed, and your loan converts to your fixed monthly mortgage.

title: Delivery & Installation
subtitle: From factory transport to crane set day: How your precision modular home is installed
content:
The Modular Delivery & Installation Journey

Modular home construction is up to 50% faster than traditional building because site preparation and factory manufacturing occur simultaneously. While your foundation is being poured and cured, your home is engineered in our climate-controlled facility.

The 4-Stage Installation Process

1. Site Foundation & Utility Pre-Work

Your local general contractor or foundation specialist pours the engineered concrete slab, crawlspace, or basement according to our certified anchor bolt plans. Plumbing and electrical utility trenches are brought to the foundation perimeter.

2. Nationwide Transport & Staging

Completed home modules are wrapped in protective weather-tight transport membranes and delivered to your site via specialized carriers accompanied by certified escort drivers.

3. Crane Set Day (The Big Reveal!)

A high-capacity mobile crane lifts each volumetric module from the trailer and sets it onto the permanent foundation with millimeter precision. Structural steel anchor plates are welded and bolted together. Most homes are fully dried-in and under roof in a single day!

4. Button-Up, Utility Hookup & Trim

Our set crew completes the module marry-wall connections, installs exterior ridge caps and siding seams, connects plumbing and electrical runs, and conducts final cosmetic touchups.

Site Access Checklist

  • Minimum 14-foot vertical clearance for delivery trailers.
  • All-weather gravel or paved access road capable of supporting 60,000+ lb trucks.
  • Permits obtained for crane staging on local roadways if required by your municipality.

title: How It Works: The Modular Building Process
subtitle: 5 simple steps from selecting your floor plan to moving into your custom modular home
content:
A Smarter, Faster Way to Build

Building a custom home should be exciting, not stressful. ModularHome.com transforms the traditional construction nightmare into a streamlined 5-step process backed by steel engineering and precision factory automation.

The 5-Step Process

Step 1: Explore & Customize Your Design

Browse our catalog of 2026 modular homes, barndominiums, house kits, and cabins. Customize floor plans, bedroom layouts, finishes, and exterior architectural aesthetics to match your land and lifestyle.

Step 2: Instant Itemized Quotation & Engineering

Receive a clear, transparent price breakdown including factory manufacturing, freight logistics, and optional turnkey installation packages. Our architectural team produces state-stamped engineering plans for your local permit office.

Step 3: Permitting & Simultaneous Site Preparation

While your local building department approves permits and your foundation is excavated and poured, your home begins assembly inside our state-of-the-art facility. No weather delays, no mold exposure, and zero material damage.

Step 4: Precision Factory Manufacturing (4–8 Weeks)

Skilled craftsmen and laser-guided framing tools assemble cold-formed steel frames, electrical wiring, plumbing, insulation, drywall, cabinetry, and fixtures in a climate-controlled environment with rigorous 120-point quality inspections.

Step 5: Rapid Delivery, Crane Assembly & Move-In

Your modules arrive on-site and are crane-lifted onto your foundation. The button-up crew seals marriage lines, connects utilities, and finishes trim work. Receive your keys in a fraction of the time of standard stick-building!

title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
subtitle: Answers to top questions about modular home building, costs, customization, and permits
content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Have questions about modular and prefab construction? Below are answers to the most common questions we receive from home buyers across the United States.

General & Construction FAQs

Are modular homes the same as manufactured or mobile homes?

No. Modular homes are built to the exact same local state and International Residential Codes (IRC/IBC) as custom site-built houses. They are permanently attached to concrete foundations and appreciate in value identically to stick-built homes. Mobile/manufactured homes are built to federal HUD code on non-removable steel chassis.

How long does the entire modular building process take?

From initial contract and permitting to final key handover, modular homes typically take 3 to 6 months—compared to 10 to 16 months for traditional stick-built homes.

Can I customize the floor plan and interior finishes?

Yes! Every plan in our catalog can be customized. You can move interior walls, add bedrooms, expand porches, upgrade to vaulted ceilings, and select custom siding, flooring, and kitchen finishes.

How do modular homes handle extreme weather and high winds?

Because modular homes must be built to withstand highway transportation and crane lifting, they are structurally stronger than stick-built homes. Our steel-framed modular models are rated for hurricane-force winds up to 150 MPH and extreme snow loads up to 50 PSF.

Who handles local building permits?

ModularHome.com provides full state-stamped architectural and structural engineering blueprint packages for your local building department. Your local general contractor or our turnkey build partner will submit these plans to your county permitting office.
